subject: Quantify.ai trial: success metrics, measurement plan & owners
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@quantify.ai>, procurement@quantify.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quantify.ai trial: success metrics, measurement plan & owners

Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Per our discovery, I captured a short, agreed-upon measurement plan we can use to run the 4-week trial and make a go/no-go recommendation. Please review and flag anything missing.

Goal: validate Redwood Inference for low-latency, cost-effective LLM enrichment in Quantify's data pipelines and measure output quality against your current baseline.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: P50 <= 180 ms and P95 <= 350 ms for 1k token requests under production-like load.
- Throughput: sustain 400 concurrent inference requests with average concurrency per worker matching observed traffic patterns (target 300–500 rps overall).
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0009 for your baseline prompt set (we'll measure tokens consumed end-to-end).
- Quality: exact-match rate >= 87% on your 250-sample labeled set and BLEU/F1 comparisons to your current model within +/- 3 points.

Measurement plan and owners:
- Redwood will provide: an instrumentation snippet and a sample Drive workbook (attached) to capture latency histograms, token counts, and output samples — owner: Ben Carter.
- Quantify will provide: a labeled prompt set (250 items) and representative production trace for load generation — owner: Alex Johnson.
- Shared: weekly syncs (Thursdays), final readout in week 5 with pass/fail recommendation. Redwood will run the trial in our dedicated sandbox account in us-west; Quantify to approve IP/egress requirements.

Deliverables we attached: trial success metrics workbook, sample prompts (anonymized), and network topology checklist.

Next steps (action items):
1) Alex: share labeled prompt set and a 24-hour production trace by EOD Fri (2027-03-19).
2) Ben: provision trial sandbox, upload instrumentation, and smoke test by Mon (2027-03-22).
3) Soojin/Marissa: schedule weekly sync invites and draft evaluation rubric by Mon.

If that aligns, we’ll treat this as the working definition of success and instrument accordingly.

Thanks,
--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: Quantify_Trial_Success_Metrics.xlsx (workbook, 42 KB); quantify_sample_prompts.jsonl (anonymized, 35 KB); network_topology_requirements.pdf (3 pages)
From: Alex Johnson <alex@quantify.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@quantify.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quantify.ai trial: success metrics, measurement plan & owners

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. Quick confirmations and a couple of clarifying questions: 

1) The latency numbers look promising. On our side, most requests average ~220 tokens. Are your cost/token targets measured including embedding generation + model tokens or just generation tokens? We want apples-to-apples.
2) For throughput, we’ll provide a 24-hr trace, but our peak burst is around 700 concurrent sec-long inference bursts. Can Redwood simulate that pattern?
3) Regarding data handling: we need confirmation on retention policy for logs and whether KV cache content will be persisted beyond the trial. Our security team also needs the network_topology_requirements.pdf filled and an expected egress/IP list.

We’ll deliver the labeled prompt set and trace by EOD Fri. Procurement copied for T&Cs they may want to start.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Product | Quantify.ai
alex@quantify.ai

On Wed, Mar 17, 2027 at 11:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Per our discovery, I captured a short, agreed-upon measurement plan we can use to run the 4-week trial and make a go/no-go recommendation. Please review and flag anything missing.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@quantify.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantify.ai trial: success metrics, measurement plan & owners

Adding technical detail from the infra/serving side so expectations are set: 

- Cost accounting: Ben (me) will instrument token counters at the Redwood API edge so the cost/token metric includes all input + output tokens for generation calls. If you use embeddings or separate calls, we will account for those separately.
- Latency measurement: we will capture client-to-response P50/P95 from the Redwood edge in the workbook and also provide per-stage breakdown (queue, model-runtime, network). That will help isolate whether tail latency is infra or model-related.
- Load pattern simulation: we can run a stress profile matching your trace, including the 700 concurrent bursts. We’ll run both steady-state and burst scenarios and include a warm-up period to ensure KV cache and batching are representative.
- KV cache: by default caches are ephemeral and tied to the trial sandbox instance; no persistent storage beyond the trial unless explicitly requested and approved by Quantify. We’ll put that in writing for procurement.

I’ll start provisioning the trial cluster today; target smoke test Mon (2027-03-22). Ben

--
Ben Carter
Infrastructure Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@quantify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@quantify.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 20:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantify.ai trial: success metrics, measurement plan & owners

Appreciate the quick turn, Alex. Confirmations below and next steps: 

- Cost basis: Ben confirmed we’ll report cost/token including input+output tokens. If you also want separate embedding accounting we’ll add that column.
- Burst simulation: we will reproduce your peak burst (700 concurrent) as part of the stress run and include a burst report in week 2.
- Data retention & KV cache: default trial retention is 7 days for logs; KV cache ephemeral to sandbox (no persistence). We’ll provide a formal retention statement for procurement this afternoon.

Action checklist update:
- Alex: deliver labeled prompts + 24-hr trace by EOD Fri (2027-03-19).
- Ben: finalize sandbox provisioning and post smoke-test notes by Mon (2027-03-22).
- Marissa: draft the trial calendar and weekly sync invites (first sync Thu 2027-03-25).
- Procurement: if you can share standard redlines up front we’ll have our legal ready to respond.

We’ll treat the attached workbook as the single source of truth for pass/fail gates; I’ll unlock edit access once your prompts are uploaded. Looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Soojin
